description: LLM Visibility (GEO) — SEO Pro addendum: AI crawler policy, product Q&A blocks, llms.txt, LLM-readiness audit, AI citation monitor, entity grounding. All gated on existing FEATURES.SEO_PRO. Source: tasks/prd-seo-llm-visibility.md.

userStories.title: AI crawler policy manager
userStories.description: As a Pro tenant, I control which AI bots read my store — search crawlers for visibility, training crawlers by choice.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/seo/ai-crawlers.ts: bot registry as data — search class (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, xAI search UA) and training class (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Google-Extended, CCBot, meta-externalagent) with owner labels; ONE source for robots rendering and the audit
Tenant setting aiCrawlerPolicy ('open'|'search-only'|'blocked', default 'open') in the validated tenant-settings shape
app/store/[slug]/robots.txt renders per-bot directives from the policy for Pro tenants; Basic tenants render today's output byte-identical (asserted)

Pro-gated UI card in the SEO Manager: policy radio + per-class copy stating plainly what each choice costs (search-blocked = absent from AI answers; training-blocked = absent from future model knowledge)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass (targeted vitest run — robots output matrix per policy x plan)
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (fallback per PROMPT)
userStories.notes: Robots route from the parent run: app/store/[slug]/robots.txt/route.ts (custom-domain aware, cached). Tenant settings shape: lib/validation/tenant-settings.ts (the parent run added businessAddress + socialLinks pattern precedent). Plan resolution: the route must read the tenant row's plan and gate via FEATURES.SEO_PRO membership (lib/entitlements — do NOT touch the Automatos keys in features.ts; #243 restored them after a merge collision). 2026 fact the copy must reflect: search and training bots are SEPARATE per provider — blocking GPTBot does not remove you from ChatGPT Search (OAI-SearchBot does).

acceptanceCriteria: Q&A stored in products.seo.qa ({question, answer}[] — Zod on all SEO PUT routes; max 10 pairs; question <=200 chars, answer <=1000; no migration)

SEO Manager product modal gains a Q&A editor (add/remove/reorder); 'Draft Q&A with Automatos AI' reuses lib/seo/ai-assist.ts with a NEW output contract (JSON array of pairs, validated, refused on violation, lands as editable draft — never auto-saved)
Product detail renders the Q&A visibly (bs-* accordion) AND as FAQPage JSON-LD through the existing lib/seo/json-ld.ts builders — both Pro-gated; Basic renders neither (asserted)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass (targeted vitest run)
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (fallback per PROMPT)
userStories.notes: entity-seo parsing: lib/seo/entity-seo.ts (fail-closed reader from parent US-003) — extend, don't fork. FAQPage builder exists (parent US-017, conditions). ai-assist provider interface: lib/seo/ai-assist.ts (parent US-024 — Automatos backend token exchange + SSE chat; tenant columns are the canonical credential store). Product detail page + its cached fetch: parent US-004's shape. Q&A prompts feed ONLY the tenant's own product content (no cross-tenant data — parent rule).

userStories.title: llms.txt generator
userStories.description: As a Pro tenant, my store publishes a clean machine-readable inventory — cheap insurance, honestly framed.
acceptanceCriteria: app/store/[slug]/llms.txt route: generated markdown — business identity + address, condition guides (title/summary/URL), top products, recent published Wire posts; primary-host URLs via storeCanonical; respects sitemapExclude/noindex from parent US-022; Cache-Control like the sitemap; works on custom domains (middleware rewrite matcher must pass .txt — it already does for robots.txt, verify llms.txt path)
Basic tenants: 404 (Pro gate); SEO Manager card copy states plainly: standards-track, ~10% adoption, no proven citation lift, zero cost
Typecheck passes
Tests pass (content shape, exclusion honoring, plan gating, host awareness)
userStories.notes: Sitemap route is the template: app/store/[slug]/sitemap.xml/route.ts (parent US-006 — filters, lastmod, caching). Middleware matcher: middleware.ts:247 region. The honesty copy is an AC, not decoration — the SE Ranking 300k-domain study found no measurable lift; the UI must not oversell.

userStories.title: LLM-readiness audit section
userStories.description: As a Pro tenant, the audit tells me what an LLM can and cannot see of my store.
acceptanceCriteria: New category in lib/seo/audit.ts: (a) search-crawler access per aiCrawlerPolicy — blocked search bots is the top-weight finding; (b) Q&A coverage across products/conditions; (c) llms.txt presence/staleness; (d) crawler-invisible blog detection: a tenant whose blog surface is the Automatos Shadow-DOM widget (wireMode column) gets a finding explaining the content is invisible to every crawler and LLM, deep-linking the Wire mode selector; (e) heading-structure quality on condition/post content
Findings carry deep links per the parent pattern; category weights documented in-code
Typecheck passes
Tests pass (each check table-driven over fixture rows)
userStories.notes: Audit engine: lib/seo/audit.ts (parent US-023 — pure checks over fetched rows, 15min cache, deep-link shape). wireMode column + the Shadow-DOM finding come from the Automatos session (their memory: 'blog widget Shadow-DOM = non-crawlable'); the mode selector UI shipped in their #240. Bot registry from US-001 is the source for check (a).

userStories.title: AI citation monitor v1
userStories.description: As a Pro tenant, I can see whether AI engines cite my store when my market asks relevant questions.
acceptanceCriteria: Model llm_citation_checks (tenantId, engine, prompt, cited Boolean, citedUrl?, mentionText?, checkedAt; @@index([tenantId, checkedAt]); tenant-scoped registration; hand-authored migration, no migrate dev)

Weekly repeatable job on its OWN queue ('llm-citation') following the reorder-reminders pattern exactly: idempotent scheduler upsert, per-tenant fault isolation (one store's failure never starves the rest), per-run cap (default 6 prompts x 2 engines per tenant), attempts: 1

Engine adapters behind ONE interface, env-key-gated: OpenAI + Perplexity first; an engine whose platform key is absent is SKIPPED and surfaced as 'not configured' in the UI — never an error. Adapters call web-search-enabled endpoints; responses scanned for the tenant's hosts (subdomain + customDomain) in cited URLs; token/cost logged per run

Prompts generated from tenant market data (country, condition topics, product categories) with medical-information framing — the rationale (engine content policies around cannabis commerce) documented in-code
Dashboard tab in the SEO Manager: per-engine cited/not-cited trend + latest mention text; empty state for unconfigured engines; Pro-gated

Worker lessons applied and journaled: own queue (email-queue expiry guard incompatibility), bypassTenantScope with tenantId in every query, Docker runner COPY check stated explicitly, touched worker files typechecked via throwaway tsconfig (scripts/ excluded from repo tsc)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass (adapter contract with mocked engines, host-match extraction incl. www/subpath forms, scheduler idempotency, key-gating, cap enforcement)
userStories.notes: The reorder-reminders pattern is the template: email run US-028 (see ralph/archive/2026-08-12-email-authoring-campaigns/progress.txt) — upsertJobScheduler fixed id, own queue, conditional-write idempotency, 5k cap, per-tenant try/catch. NEVER log or echo API keys; secrets are env names only. API spend is real: cap hard, log cost. Engine SDKs: prefer plain fetch against documented REST endpoints over adding SDK dependencies (zero-dep precedent from the parent run). If NO platform keys exist in env at build time that is FINE — everything ships key-gated with the not-configured state; do not block on missing keys.
